title: Nacha 2026 false-pretenses fraud monitoring is already binding on every non-consumer Originator but is recorded only as a '[S] contractual' row
description: OB-43 records 'Nacha 2026 fraud-monitoring rules via ODFI agreement' with no control. Nacha Phase 1 (2026-03-20) covered ODFIs and Originators >6m entries; Phase 2 (2026-06-19, practically 2026-06-22) removed the threshold for all non-consumer Originators, TPSPs and TPSs. They must establish risk-based processes reasonably intended to identify entries suspected unauthorized or authorized under False Pretenses (BEC, vendor impersonation) and review them at least annually. A sponsor originating CCD grant credits or contribution debits is a non-consumer Originator; an administrator transmitting files may be a TPS/TPSP.
impact: First live ACH origination after the PAY-DEF-001 gate would breach ODFI agreement terms if no documented program and annual review exist.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-XIN-BNK-002 (documented program, typology, annual review evidence) and UNB-XIN-BNK-001 (rail obligation register).
decision_owner: Sponsor CFO + compliance owner; counsel for Originator-of-record question

title: Recurring contribution debits from consumer accounts lack Reg E §1005.10(b) authorization and copy obligations, which bind the sponsor as payee
description: 12 CFR 1005.10(b): preauthorized EFTs from a consumer account may be authorized only by a writing signed or similarly authenticated by the consumer, and the person that obtains the authorization shall provide a copy. Comment 10(b)-2 places the violation on a third-party payee that fails to do so. §1005.10(d) puts varying-amount notice on the designated payee. Unbound's recurring requirements cover grant schedules, not inbound debit authorizations. Reg E's other duties (error resolution) sit with the donor's bank, not the sponsor.
impact: Regulatory exposure and R10 return liability for every recurring donor debit without retrievable authorization.

title: WEB debit account validation before first use is a Nacha requirement absent from contribution intake
description: Originators of WEB debits must use a commercially reasonable fraudulent-transaction detection system that includes account validation before first use of an account number and on any change. Methods include prenote, micro-entries, third-party validation. Contribution intake requirements do not mention it.
impact: Unvalidated WEB debits risk ODFI enforcement and higher R03/R04/R10 returns.

title: Card contribution disputes and chargebacks have no lifecycle; they collide with irrevocable acceptance and issued acknowledgments
description: Card networks let cardholders dispute generally within 120 days (some reasons up to 540). The acquirer debits the merchant (sponsor) provisionally on dispute; outcome depends on representment. REQ-X-009 models returns, not two-phase disputes with evidence deadlines and possible re-credit. UNB-RCN-FIN-013 forbids refunds after acceptance but a chargeback is involuntary; nothing tells the ledger which applies.

title: Provisional window is defined only by ACH R10 (≈60 days) while actual windows vary by rail, SEC code and account type
description: TVR-CON-001 cites Nacha R10. Business-account unauthorized debits use R29 with a 2-banking-day window; consumer R10/R11 use 60 days; card disputes 120 days and up to 540; ACH credits pushed by donors are not debit-reversible; wires are final on acceptance. A single window either over-restricts corporate/wire gifts or under-protects card gifts.
impact: Mis-sized capacity holds; donor friction or loss exposure.
proposed_resolution: Refine TVR-CON-001 (RR-TVR-CON-001-r1) into a versioned per-rail ReversalWindow table.

title: No requirement makes every bank-account debit match an authorized platform instruction
description: TVR-PAY-004 forbids origination outside the gate; rev3 B19 matches custodian movements daily and only 'reviews' bank-portal entitlements. Preventive rules are not detective: a staff member or compromised portal user can key a wire or ACH in the bank portal and nothing in Unbound flags it until month-end.
impact: Out-of-band payments evade every platform control; disclosed nonprofit losses are of exactly this redirection type.

title: Check issue-file transmission is not a gate before print/mail release; payee-name positive pay is not required
description: RCF-GRT-020 noted positive-pay issue/void files missing; GRT-005 covers void acknowledgment only. If a check is mailed before the bank acknowledges the issue file, positive pay cannot stop an altered or counterfeit item. Mail-theft check washing alters payee names; amount-only positive pay misses it.
impact: Check fraud losses on the dominant legacy rail.

title: Unclaimed-property rule for uncashed grant checks requires a per-state table with holder/owner priority and exemptions, not one 'jurisdiction-specific dormancy rule'
description: States differ: some exempt business-to-business outstanding checks (VA per secondary source) and others explicitly do not (NY). Charitable payees are organizations, so B2B exemptions may apply; owner-address priority determines which state. Whether voiding a stale grant check extinguishes property owed to the charity is unsettled (REG-045). GRT-005 says 'jurisdiction-specific dormancy rule' without the table fields.
impact: Under- or over-reporting; or funds silently re-credited.

title: Securities gift intake lacks a deterministic DTC delivery-matching contract; 'ACATS' framing is wrong for gifts
description: FINRA Rule 11870 ACATS governs customer account transfers between members and allows exception where account title mismatches; a gift changes owner and normally moves by non-ACATS DTC delivery. The competitive matrix lists 'ACATS/DTC mechanics unknown'. Unidentified deliveries are left to AI-suggested matching.
impact: Misattributed gifts (wrong donor's acknowledgment), delayed acceptance.

title: Payment deferral gate lists 'fraud operations' as a future decision, but several obligations bind from the first live contribution or grant, regardless of provider
description: UNB-PAY-008 defers fraud operations, limits and rail eligibility. Reg E §1005.10(b), Nacha WEB validation, Nacha fraud monitoring and PCI scope bind as soon as the sponsor accepts debits/cards or originates ACH. The gate needs explicit binding prerequisites.
impact: Risk of going live with a selected provider but no compliant obligations.

title: No account-level cash position and disbursement prefunding forecast
description: Per-grant funding states exist, but ACH credit files debit the Originator on settlement date, checks clear unpredictably and liquidation proceeds arrive T+1. Nothing projects whether each disbursement account will cover the day's releases.
impact: Overdrafts, rejected files, rushed liquidations or delayed grants.

title: Donor-covered processing fees: acknowledgment amount, gross/net recognition and fee evidence undefined
description: Many giving platforms let donors 'cover the fee'. The gross charged is the contribution; the processor deducts fees from payouts. FeeBase covers fees charged to funds, not processor fees on inbound gifts. Without a rule, the acknowledgment may show net, or the fund may be credited gross while cash is net.
impact: Incorrect acknowledgments and unreconcilable processor payouts.

title: No defense against card-testing (enumeration) attacks on public or embedded contribution forms
description: Low-friction donation forms are used to test stolen cards with small authorizations; each attempt incurs authorization fees and later chargebacks/fraud reports that damage acquirer standing.
impact: Fee leakage, acquirer termination, dispute ratios.

title: ACH return-rate thresholds and reinitiation rules are not monitored
description: Nacha unauthorized debit return threshold is 0.5%, administrative return level 3.0%, overall 15.0%. Reinitiated entries must keep same Company Name, ID and amount with 'RETRY PYMT'; unauthorized returns cannot be reinitiated. No requirement monitors rates or constrains retries for contribution debits.
impact: ODFI inquiry/fines; loss of origination capability for the sponsor.

title: Rail eligibility is not stated per payment class; contributions, grants, administrative fees and investment transactions need different rails and reversibility
description: REQ-X-083 is grant-centric. Admin fees are internal journals (no rail); investment transactions move via custodian; contributions are inbound pulls or pushes; returns of unaccepted property are outbound to donors. A single matrix (payment class x rail x direction x irreversibility class x allowed) removes ambiguity and keeps instant rails off by default.
impact: Accidental use of irrevocable rails or of donor-refund paths for grants.

title: Payment events do not emit cost-to-serve drivers
description: Exception management tracks cost per resolved case, but per-rail costs (provider fees, check print/postage, lockbox, manual touches, exceptions) are not emitted as facts the economics model can consume.
impact: Pricing and rail-steering decisions without data.

title: Risk of importing bank CIP/CDD workflows into donor onboarding
description: Sponsor is not a covered FI; CDD duties fall on its banks, which (for a nonprofit legal-entity customer) need only control-prong data, now without per-account re-verification (FIN-2026-R001). The only CDD-like artifact the sponsor needs is its own signer/control-person register for bank onboarding.
impact: Unnecessary donor friction and PII retention.

title: Administrator-as-intermediary funds flow can make a vendor a Third-Party Sender or money transmitter
description: If contribution or grant funds settle through an administrator/vendor account rather than the sponsor's, Nacha TPS obligations and state money-transmission questions (REG-042/043) arise; Givinga's 'external bank fraud loss' illustrates processor-sponsor exposure.
impact: Licensing exposure and unclear liability for losses.
proposed_resolution: Decision XID-BNK-005: funds must settle directly to sponsor-titled accounts by default.

title: Posting idempotency keyed by posting-rule version permits re-posting history when a rule changes
description: ACC-MDL-007 makes posting idempotent 'per event, accounting book and posting-rule version'. A new rule version is a new idempotency key, so replaying events after a rule change produces a second journal for the same event. UNB-NAV-044/UNB-IMM-005 require deterministic projection rebuild, which, if applied to the journal itself, recomputes issued periods under current code. Nothing states that posted journals are persisted facts that rebuilds may not regenerate.
impact: Auditor-tested balances for a closed year can differ from a rebuilt ledger after a code or policy change; double posting on replay; restatement without authority.
proposed_resolution: Refine ACC-MDL-007 (RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1): idempotency per (source event, book); rule-version changes only via the accounting-change protocol (UNB-XIN-ACC-004); add re-derivation as a detective control (UNB-XIN-ACC-003).

title: Grant recognition point is undecided and conditional grants have no barrier tracking
description: ASC 720-25-25-1 requires contributions made to be expensed in the period made; unconditional promises to give are payables. ASU 2018-08 defines a condition as barrier plus right of return/release and presumes ambiguous promises conditional. A large sponsor's audited policy records unconditional grants 'when they are approved' and conditional grants when conditions are substantially met. Unbound leaves the point to OD-19 with no parameter, no evidence that the promise was communicated, and no state for barrier-bearing grants (multi-year, matching, milestone).
impact: Year-end approved-unpaid grants (December surge) cannot be cut off consistently; Schedule D grants and GAAP grant expense diverge.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ACC-002: sponsor-level recognition-point parameter with communication evidence and a ConditionalGrant state; recommend approval-plus-communication as default for CPA review.

title: Agency funds and donor-designated pass-through gifts are not modeled
description: Community-foundation and hybrid sponsors hold agency endowments and designations for other nonprofits, which ASC 958-605 treats as liabilities (reciprocal transfers), not contributions. Workplace or embedded giving where the donor designates a specific charity may be pass-through. No Unbound requirement selects liability posting for these account types or excludes them from Schedule D DAF figures.
impact: Contribution revenue and DAF aggregates overstated for hybrid/embedded sponsors.

UNB-ACC-017 names 'adjusting entries' only. Without an audit-adjustment period, AJEs either reopen December (breaking issued donor statements) or land in January (wrong year).
impact: Audited statements cannot be reproduced from the ledger; donor statements and audited statements diverge without an explanation.

title: Accounting changes (principle, estimate, error) have no classification or mechanism

The requirements only say closed periods stay immutable.

TVC-027 recorded the contradiction; GAP-016 lists it; no requirement exists.

title: One case model is right, one case lifecycle is harmful
description: RCF-PLT-025 proposes 'one Case aggregate with typed case kinds sharing one lifecycle and routing' and RR-REQ-X-057-r1 requires 'one case model'. Sharing identity, subject links, ownership, routing, timeline and audit is sound. Sharing one lifecycle, one SLA clock semantics, one permission set and one retention/hold rule is not: a complaint response clock, a sanctions investigation (no external clock, restricted access, 10-year OFAC retention), a reconsideration (independence rule) and a payment Unknown exception (auto-closes on provider evidence) have incompatible closure, visibility and retention semantics.
impact: Either every kind inherits the strictest rules (over-restriction, over-retention, complaint staff cannot see their own cases) or the weakest (investigations visible to service staff; holds lost on case purge).
proposed_resolution: Adopt a case kernel with per-kind policy profiles (UNB-XIN-SVC-002): kernel = identity, kind, subjects, owner/assignee, routing, timeline, evidence refs, commitments, audit; profile = state set and closure rule, clock policy, access class, retention/hold binding, outcome set, independence rule, auto-close permission. Domain state stays in subject aggregates.

title: WorkItem creation rule excludes customer-initiated requests
description: RR-REQ-X-048-r1 allows a WorkItem only for (a) rule hold, (b) missing/conflicting evidence, (c) decision requiring human authority, (d) provider Unknown. A donor complaint, a reconsideration request (UNB-RCN-ENT-016), a correction request or a question the corpus cannot answer is none of these unless forced into (c). Strict reading leaves customer-initiated work with no lawful container.
impact: Complaints and reconsiderations either go untracked or are mislabelled as authority decisions, corrupting STP metrics (UNB-RCN-PLT-006).
proposed_resolution: Refine to RR-REQ-X-048-r2 adding cause (e): a request or complaint from an authenticated or identified external party that requires a human response, still with exit condition and creating source.

evidence: unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/IVR-TELEPHONE-SELF-SERVICE-NUMERIC-IDENTIFIERS-2026-11-23.md:45;unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/DOCUMENT-CLASSIFICATION-RETENTION-MATRIX-AND-DISPOSITION-GOVERNANCE-2026-11-23.md:26;https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/2511 (accessed 2026-11-23);https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2023/934.03 (accessed 2026-11-23);https://ktslaw.com/en/Blog/GlobalPrivacy-and-CybersecurityLaw/2024/7/Wiretap-Laws-in-the-United-States (search-result summary only; page not fully read) (accessed 2026-11-23)
title: No recording or transcription consent requirement
description: Federal law permits recording with one party's consent (18 USC 2511(2)(d)); Florida requires all parties' prior consent (Fla. Stat. 934.03(2)(d)); California and roughly 9-12 other states are commonly listed as all-party consent states (counts vary by source). The IVR spec defers recording to 'legal review' and TEL-01 retention is TBD. Caller location cannot be determined reliably, so per-state logic is unsafe. AI transcription by a vendor adds a further third-party processing question (counsel).
impact: Unlawful recording exposure in all-party states; recordings of DTMF secrets; unretained evidence.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-SVC-003: universal disclosure and consent before any recording or machine transcription, unrecorded alternative, pause for secrets, vendor contract review; counsel decision XID-SVC-002.

title: No definition separating contact, case, transaction and exception
description: Nothing states when an interaction is just a contact, when it becomes a case, or that a financial transaction is never itself a case. 'Unified intake' (ADM-015) and 'every multi-step goal has a case' (AIN-009) push toward case-per-contact; RR-REQ-X-048-r1 pushes toward no case for customer requests.
impact: Queue inflation or invisible work; double state machines for transactions; meaningless cost-per-case metrics.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-SVC-001 typed interaction classes and promotion rules.

title: Complaint is undefined; no acknowledgement or response clocks
description: Complaints appear in topic lists and a control row but are never defined, so a dissatisfied email about a slow grant is an inquiry unless the donor uses the word. No acknowledgement deadline, response deadline, regulator-originated path or closure root cause exists. External benchmark: CFPB expects company responses generally within 15 days and final responses within 60 (not binding on charities).
impact: Under-counted complaints; AG/IRS complaints handled as routine; no learning.
decision_owner: Head of Client and Partner Operations

title: Service quality metrics named but undefined
description: ADM-042 lists user effort, time to resolution, repeated contacts and outcome with no formulas, denominators or windows. Deflection is not defined anywhere; landscape targets (status contacts -70%) have no baseline method.
impact: Unverifiable claims of AI-native service savings.

title: Surge sizing covers deferrable backlog only, not real-time channels
description: The economic model sizes December exception backlog with a k multiplier and backlog arithmetic. Real-time contacts (calls, chat) abandon rather than queue for days and must be sized to a service level by interval (Erlang-C/A). Illustrative computation (10-min handle, 80% answered in 60 s): 15 calls/h needs 5 agents (50% occupancy), 45 calls/h needs 11, 90 calls/h needs 19. Small pools run at low occupancy, so a small sponsor offering live phone in December pays a high cost per contact. December concentration is evidenced: Vanguard ~22% of CY2024 grants by count in December; Daffy ~43% of 2025 contributions in December.
impact: Abandoned year-end calls translate to missed tax-year gifts and complaints; or overstaffing all year.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-SVC-008 seasonal capacity plan converting real-time to scheduled callback/async where possible.
decision_owner: Head of Client and Partner Operations

title: Promises made to customers are not tracked
description: Callbacks and promised dates live in free-text notes (REQ-X-024 'follow-up references'). No due date, owner or pre-breach alert.
impact: Broken commitments are a common complaint driver (general industry knowledge, unverified).

title: Transcripts and AI summaries could be mistaken for instructions
description: A summary stating 'donor asked to grant $20k to X' could be acted on by staff. UNB-RCN-GRT-010 requires explicit affirmative action with affirmation evidence for grant submission, but no rule prevents a transcript or summary being used as the basis of a staff-entered action.
impact: Social engineering via phone + summary; hallucinated instructions.

title: No governed, versioned donor-facing answer corpus
description: Landscape design depends on a GC-approved clause corpus; Unbound requirements cover AI guidance for configuration but not versioned customer-facing answers, so a past answer cannot be reconstructed or corrected when policy changes.
impact: Inconsistent answers; misleading-statement exposure; inability to notify donors who received a superseded answer.

title: No assurance-by-channel disclosure and action matrix for assisted contacts
description: UNB-RCN-ENT-016 makes staff-entered consequential actions pending verified-channel confirmation, but what staff may disclose (balance, grant list, charity names, payment status) at each assurance level is undecided (IVR open decision 4). Knowledge questions using facts available from statements, data brokers or the charity itself provide weak assurance.
impact: Information leakage enabling later takeover; inconsistent agent behaviour.

title: Sticky owner routing and real-time supervision are over-specified for live contacts
description: Routing live contacts to a named owner makes response time depend on one person; supervisor barge/wallboard features presume large pools.
impact: Build cost without benefit at DAF volumes.
proposed_resolution: Live contacts go to any qualified agent and generate an owner follow-up Commitment; keep asynchronous oversight only (see XRJ-SVC-002).

title: Reconsideration lacks independence, filing window, de novo review and scope
description: UNB-RCN-ENT-016 defines outcome set, owner and response time only. Claims law offers a tested pattern: ERISA 29 CFR 2560.503-1(h) requires no deference to the initial decision, a reviewer neither the original decider nor a subordinate, at least 180 days to file (group health) and decision deadlines. It also does not separate shared charity-vetting reconsideration (platform record) from a sponsor's grant decision.
impact: Original reviewer rubber-stamps own decision; unbounded reopen requests; a charity's challenge to platform vetting changes a sponsor grant decision without sponsor authority.

title: No content standard for adverse or conditional decision notices
description: Gates produce reason codes and AIN-025 explains blocks in UI, but no requirement defines what a donor or charity is told when a recommendation is declined, held or conditioned: specific reason, policy reference, what evidence would change it, how to request reconsideration, and what must not be disclosed (sanctions/investigation).
impact: Unexplained declines drive contacts and complaints; inconsistent disclosure of screening details.

title: No decision-time commitments per decision type
description: Prior-authorization rules (CMS-0057-F: 72h expedited, 7 calendar days standard, public metrics) show the value of declared decision clocks. DAF requirements have SLAs in general but no per-decision-type decision-time target (grant recommendation, gift acceptance, charity onboarding, reconsideration) nor publication of p50/p90.
impact: Unpredictable waits, 'where is my grant' contacts.

title: Information requests have no deadline, tolling or duplicate-ask prevention
description: WaitingForEvidence has no due date, reminder cadence, effect on decision clock or disposition when unanswered. AIN-007 says reuse verified evidence but nothing enforces a check of the evidence registry before asking. NAIC Model 900 Sec.4(K) treats requiring duplicate verification as an unfair claims practice; the same friction applies to donors and charities.
impact: Indefinitely pended cases; repeated document requests; inflated handle time.

title: No restricted investigation case kind; investigator and adjudicator not separated
description: Suspected fraud, related-party diversion or sanctions matters escalate (UNB-GEX-033) into general queues. Nothing restricts the case to need-to-know staff, hides it from the subject's service view and from the AI assistant context, or prevents the investigator from also making the sponsor decision.
impact: Tipping off the subject; leakage to service staff; biased decisions; litigation exposure.

title: No decision-quality sampling of automated approvals
description: Metrics push straight-through processing up (UNB-RCN-PLT-006) and count false positives (UNB-GEX-023) but nothing samples STP approvals for false negatives (approved but should have held). Insurers run closed-file leakage audits for this reason.
impact: Silent eligibility errors accumulate; STP rate becomes a perverse incentive.

title: No protective path when a representative may be exploiting the donor
description: HIPAA 164.502(g)(5) lets a covered entity decline to treat a person as personal representative on reasonable belief of abuse or endangerment. DAF representatives (POA, family advisors) have no analogous protective suspension; ADM-045 only says not to assume incapacity.
impact: Elder financial exploitation through grants to related or sham charities.

title: Reopen semantics conflict between decisions and work cases
description: SM-0: terminal objects never reopen; later facts create linked child records. UNB-GEX-023 measures 'reopened cases' and EXC-18 creates a 'reopening case'. Both are right for different things.
impact: Implementers apply one rule to both, either mutating decisions or spawning case chains for simple follow-ups.
proposed_resolution: Kernel rule in UNB-XIN-SVC-002: decision aggregates follow SM-0; work cases may reopen within the profile's reopen window with versioned history, after which a linked case is created.

title: Privileged legal material has no access class
description: Legal holds are covered; attorney-client privileged notes in cases are not distinguished and could be exported (Folio dossiers, UNB-GEX-027) or fed to AI context.
impact: Privilege waiver.

title: Outsourced service staff are not a modelled principal type
description: Outsourced-admin and white-label models may use BPO staff. REQ-X-073 covers vendor SOC assurance but not per-vendor permission profiles, QA attribution, or immediate revocation on vendor offboarding.
impact: Over-privileged vendor staff; inability to attribute errors.

title: Handoffs per outcome are not measured
description: Healthcare prior-auth automation targets the elimination of handoffs; Unbound measures human touches (UNB-RCN-PLT-006) but not handoffs between people/teams, which drive latency.
impact: Cradle-to-grave ownership benefits unmeasured.

title: Fee period segmentation, proration and minimum-fee shortfall unspecified
description: The FeeBase contract declares minimums but not how periods split on open/close/transfer/schedule change, how minimums prorate, or what happens when a minimum exceeds the available balance.
impact: Double charges at migration (TVS-308), negative balances, inconsistent statements.

title: No payer-source distinction for fees
description: 'Billing, collections' does not distinguish fund-deducted fees, donor-paid memberships and partner invoices. A donor-paid membership routed through intake could be acknowledged as a contribution.
impact: Tax substantiation error; misposted partner fees.

title: Operator billing to tenants not separated from tenant ledgers
description: Model C/D operator charges are part of 'fee waterfall' prose; no rule keeps operator revenue out of sponsor books or requires pass-through disclosure.
impact: Sponsor books contain operator-originated entries; undisclosed pass-through.

title: No guard separating operating-vendor payees from grant recipients
description: Excluding operating AP natively leaves no rule preventing a vendor being paid via the grant path, or a charity that sells services to the donor or sponsor receiving a disguised payment.
impact: Prohibited benefit; misuse of charitable assets.

title: Threshold splitting is a test name without a rule
description: No aggregation key, window or cumulative limit is defined.
impact: Approval limits can be evaded.

title: Cost-to-serve named as a metric with no data
description: Work items lack program/segment/balance-band dimensions and effort categories.
impact: No relationship profitability input.

title: Fee and relationship events not classified by authority
description: Ontology lists a fee lifecycle and says the fee engine is authoritative over partner billing, but there is no event-class rule preventing CRM or partner messages from acting as financial facts.
impact: Shadow ledgers in integrations.

title: ERP scope remains normative in source files despite RCD-013
description: The original UNB-ACC-012..014 and UNB-GAP-027 still read as native obligations (AP, AR, budgeting, procurement, staffing). Only RR-UNB-ACC-012-r1 narrows AP. AR and budgeting are not narrowed; ADM-028 is the only fee-specific line.
impact: Scope creep toward an ERP.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RCD-013; add refinements for UNB-ACC-013 (AR only for partner invoices) and UNB-ACC-014 (exclude) in the integrator's pass; see XRJ-ERP-001..004.

title: Vendor assurance has no freshness or CUEC rule
description: REQ-X-073 lists topics only.
impact: Reliance on expired or out-of-scope SOC reports.

title: Fee administration line is not testable
description: ADM-028 says 'review fee schedules, accruals...' with no lifecycle, idempotency or waiver rule.
impact: Untestable fee runs.

title: Shared party model lacks capacity-scoped PII
description: ONT-1 separates capacities but nothing prevents a single party record from exposing donor data to staff serving the same person as charity contact or professional advisor.
impact: PII disclosure; anonymity breach.

title: Affiliation edges that feed TVCTL-14 are never captured
description: The excess-benefit gate depends on a relationship graph; onboarding does not collect officer/employee/director affiliations, and organization-advised funds (charity as holder) are not classified.
impact: Self-dealing undetected.

title: Communications rules omit sender entity, opt-out timing and nonprofit/for-profit regime
description: CAN-SPAM duties (postal address, 10-business-day opt-out, designated sender) and TCPA consent levels depend on the sender entity; in white-label programs the sender may be a for-profit partner.
impact: Statutory violations.

title: Segmentation on grant categories exposes sensitive inferences
description: No restriction on using religion/health/political inferences.
impact: Privacy harm, reputational risk.

title: No fund-level servicing model or coverage
description: HNW programs promise named contacts.
impact: Stalled service.

title: Referral compensation outside fund assets ungoverned
description: Paid solicitor/fundraiser registration may apply to referral compensation.
impact: State registration exposure.

title: Professional advisor changing firms not handled
description: Access and fees may persist after departure.
impact: Unauthorized access.

title: Household concept underspecified relative to CRM practice
description: CRM householding drives pricing breakpoints and combined statements; ADM-008 should state that households confer no pricing aggregation or access.
impact: Pressure to aggregate.

title: Charitable beneficiaries not revalidated at activation
description: Decades may pass between designation and activation.
impact: Grant to dissolved charity.

title: Legacy intent not stored as non-binding record
description: Letter of wishes noted in ontology only.
impact: Lost stewardship context or wrongful restrictions.

title: Entity/trust holders and entity termination
description: Signatory changes vs succession undefined.
impact: Mis-processed succession.

title: Representative scope over advisory privileges and restoration undefined
description: Whether POA agents can recommend grants is a legal question; no restoration path.
impact: Unauthorized recommendations.

title: Successor response window missing
description: Fidelity uses 90 days; requirements silent.
impact: Funds stuck.

title: No consented family-office feed
description: ADM-044 covers in-app views only.
impact: Ad hoc exports.

title: No precedence rules for conflicting instructions
description: ADM-023 holds on conflict but never defines what a conflict is; standing recurring instructions vs later recommendations, co-advisor disagreement, and plan versions all defer to 'policy'. AUTH-I4 defines 'require all' only for joint successors.
impact: Inconsistent outcomes; silent last-writer-wins.

title: Succession limits vary widely and should be configuration only
description: SVCF caps at 3 successors, CCT 2 generations, FFTC 1 generation by default, NPT/Vanguard perpetual. Hard-coding any cap would be wrong.
impact: Rigid model.
proposed_resolution: Keep UNB-SUCC-005 as configuration; add fixtures for each published policy.

title: Equivalency-determination route is unspecified and its legal basis was recorded as low-confidence
description: UNB-GRANT-041 says 'equivalency/expenditure-responsibility ... as applicable'; REQ-X-065 lists ED routes but no data. OB-20 marks ED for DAFs 'unsettled' (low). Rev. Proc. 2017-53 §2 states sponsors of DAFs may use its guidelines for the §4966(c)(2)(A) exception until further guidance, and the 2023 NPRM would codify ED for DAFs. Currency is computable: written advice is current while the law is unchanged and facts are from the grantee's current or prior taxable year (up to about two years); public-support advice is current for the two taxable years after the five-year test period. Advice must come from a qualified tax practitioner (attorney, CPA, enrolled agent).
impact: Without an ED record and computed expiry, foreign grants either route to costly ER or are paid on stale advice (taxable distribution exposure, 20% sponsor tax).
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-XIN-NPG-001 (ED case with computed currency) and RR-UNB-GRANT-041-r1; upgrade OB-20 confidence (see XRA-001).

title: US-intermediary route for international recommendations is not modelled
description: Top-50 sponsors sent $215.6m to nine named cross-border intermediaries in FY2023-24 (CAF America $58.6m from 30 sponsors) and $432.9m to 'friends of' organizations, versus $1.891bn of direct foreign grants. Unbound treats international grants only as ED/ER cases.
impact: Sponsors without ED/ER capability (most D2C, white-label, high-volume-low-balance models) must decline international recommendations or build costly diligence.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-XIN-NPG-002: sponsor-configured intermediary catalogue offered when a foreign recipient lacks a current ED and the sponsor does not offer ER.

title: Fiscal-sponsorship evidence and conduit test are undefined
description: Requirements separate fiscal sponsor, project and payee but define no accepted evidence (agreement type, sponsor's control/discretion over funds) and no check that the project is not an individual or for-profit receiving funds through the sponsor. Fiscal sponsors carry 4.0-4.4x their count share in dollars among non-routine recipients.
impact: A fiscal sponsor passes the BMF check while funds pass through to a non-charitable payee; or every fiscal-sponsor grant goes to manual review.

title: Grant data needed for Form 990 Schedules I and F is not captured
description: RR-REQ-X-060-r1 defines a Schedule D Part I package only. Schedule I requires per-recipient grants over $5,000 (name, address, EIN, IRC section, cash, noncash, purpose). Schedule F requires foreign grants by region, purpose, manner of cash disbursement (wire/ACH/check) and a description of ED/ER procedures. Region and manner-of-disbursement are not attributes of the grant model.
impact: Annual filing assembled manually; misreported foreign activity.

title: Charity organizational changes have no defined effect on open and recurring grants
description: UNB-CHAR-004 models merger, dissolution, reinstatement, name and EIN change as history only; EXC-01/EXC-02 are generic. Missing: which events continue automatically (name change, same EIN), which require payee substitution approval (merger/successor), which cancel (dissolution), and how a retroactive reinstatement (Rev. Proc. 2014-11; applications within 15 months) releases holds.
impact: Either unnecessary manual holds for benign changes or unsafe auto-substitution of payee.

title: Sponsor discretionary holds lack criteria, expiry and consistency evidence
description: In 2026 three national sponsors restricted grants to one charity after an indictment, and 16 state AGs wrote to them on 2026-05-21 about the decision 'to stop or restrict payments'. Unbound supports restricted lists (UNB-CHAR-031) and sponsor overlay holds (DKS-GRT-004) but no board-approved criteria, evidence standard (allegation vs adjudication per UNB-EXT-005), review date or consistency report.
impact: Inconsistent or undocumented discretionary holds invite AG inquiries and donor disputes; indefinite holds strand fund value.

evidence: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-30/html/2026-20026.htm Temp. Reg. §1.530A-7T(e)(2)(i)-(ii) and (f) (DAF distribution as general funding contribution is not a §4966 natural-person distribution; treated as ER exercised; applies TY beginning on/after 2026-01-01; expires 2029-09-30) (accessed 2026-11-23);unbound:requirements/reconciliation/2026-11-23/data/gap-requirements.jsonl:45-63
title: Recipient-class rule rejects all natural-person benefit, but a 2026 temporary regulation allows a DAF route to Trump accounts
description: Temp. Reg. §1.530A-7T(e)(2) (FR 2026-20026, 2026-09-30) says a 501(c)(3) furthers exempt purposes by a general funding contribution 'including ... through a distribution from a donor advised fund', that it is 'neither ... a distribution to a natural person for purposes of section 4966', and that the donor is treated as exercising expenditure responsibility. Applies to taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01; expires 2029-09-30. UNB-RCN-GRT-001 has no class for it.
impact: Product cannot offer a lawful vehicle; or staff force it through class (f) override.

title: No workflow when a taxable distribution, prohibited benefit or excess-benefit payment is discovered after payment
description: All controls are preventive. Nothing captures the incident, the attempt to recover (§4958 correction), the knowing-manager analysis, Form 4720 inputs, Schedule L reporting or board notification. Form 4720 appears only in OB-15.
impact: Late or missing excise-tax filings; uncorrected excess benefits (second-tier taxes).

title: Grantee acknowledgment collection is bundled with onboarding and bank verification
description: UNB-GRANT-026 combines four controls of different necessity. A DAF sponsor needs no receipt from the grantee; settlement evidence proves delivery, and a charity receipt risks a deductible-gift receipt to the donor (handled by UNB-RCN-GRT-011). REQ-X-058 warns against forcing registration before every grant.
impact: Chasing receipts adds nonprofit burden and queue work with no legal benefit.

evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/53.4945-5 (b)(1), (b)(3) signed grantee commitment terms, (c) annual reports, (c)(3)(i) 4-year records, (a)(5) good faith determination (accessed 2026-11-23);unbound:requirements/grants/END-TO-END-GRANT-LIFECYCLE-AND-OPERATING-MODEL.md:39,41,56
title: 'Support grant agreements' does not say when an agreement is legally required
description: Only ER grants need a written commitment signed by a grantee officer with specified terms (§53.4945-5(b)(3)). Routine grants to public charities can carry unilateral award terms.
impact: Either agreements are imposed on all grants (cost, friction) or omitted for ER grants (taxable distribution).
proposed_resolution: Refine as RR-UNB-GRANT-024-r1 with three tiers.

evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/78dd-2 (h)(1) 'domestic concern' includes any corporation ... association ... unincorporated organization organized under US state law (accessed 2026-11-23);https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-11-14/html/2023-24982.htm preamble and proposed foreign-organization distributee paragraph (good faith determination using procedures similar to §53.4945-5(a)(5); foreign governments treated as §170(b)(1)(A) if exclusively public purposes) (accessed 2026-11-23)
title: International grants lack anti-bribery and foreign-government grantee handling
description: FCPA 'domestic concern' covers US-organized nonprofits. The NPRM would treat foreign governments as §170(b)(1)(A) organizations if the distribution is exclusively for public purposes, but that is proposed only.
impact: Grants benefiting foreign officials; misclassified government grantees.

evidence: https://govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2022-12-21/html/2022-27639.htm (humanitarian/NGO general licenses across programs, 87 FR 78484; search-result summary, text not read) (accessed 2026-11-23)
title: Screening scope has no license basis for lawful humanitarian grants into sanctioned jurisdictions
description: OFAC's 2022 humanitarian and NGO general licenses authorize some activity in programs that otherwise prohibit it. UNB-RCN-GRT-007 defines subjects/lists/triggers but no license-basis record; so such grants can only be blocked or overridden.
impact: Either lawful humanitarian grants are refused, or staff override without documented authority.

evidence: https://www.iofm.com/ask-the-expert/handling-uncashed-donation-checks-and-escheatment (tax-exempt holders not exempt; secondary; search-result summary) (accessed 2026-11-23);unverified — general industry knowledge
title: Unclaimed-property jurisdiction for stale grant checks is not determinable
description: UNB-RCN-GRT-005 references 'the jurisdiction-specific dormancy rule' but not how the jurisdiction is chosen. Under the US Supreme Court priority rules (Texas v. New Jersey, 1965 — general knowledge) the first claim belongs to the state of the owner's (payee charity's) last known address, the second to the holder's state of incorporation. Tax-exempt holders are generally not exempt; some states exempt business-to-business property.
impact: Reports to the wrong state; missed due-diligence letters.

title: Restricted-purpose monitoring for public-charity grants is treated as if it were a §4966 control
description: §4966(c)(2)(A) excepts distributions to §170(b)(1)(A) organizations (other than disqualified SOs) without regard to purpose; purpose monitoring of such grants is sponsor policy. Legal purpose limits that remain: the sponsor's own exempt status (e.g. political campaign) and §4967 benefits, already handled by RR-UNB-GRANT-011-r1.
impact: Unnecessary monitoring cost and nonprofit reporting burden.
proposed_resolution: Record as sponsor policy (decision XID-NPG-006); keep REQ-X-069 optional.

evidence: https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/administrative_ruling/FIN-2014-R009.pdf (payment-processor exemption 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5)(ii)(B) conditions; search-result summary, ruling not read in full) (accessed 2026-11-23);unbound:requirements/reconciliation/2026-11-23/05-COMPETITIVE-COVERAGE-MATRIX.md:100,113;unbound:requirements/DAF-LANDSCAPE-CONVERSION-WAVE-05.md:24
title: No requirement fixes who holds legal title to disbursement funds; a vendor-held float can make the operator a money transmitter
description: If the for-profit platform operator receives sponsor money into its own accounts and transmits it to charities, state money-transmission licensing and FinCEN MSB registration questions arise. The FinCEN payment-processor exemption conditions (as summarised) concern payment for goods or services through BSA-regulated clearing systems; a charitable grant is neither. Failures in the corpus (Flipcause: CA AG cease order then Chapter 7; SDG Impact Fund: receivership) involved commingling.
impact: Licensing exposure for the operator; insolvency risk to charitable money; sponsor reputational harm.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-XIN-REG-001: sponsor-titled accounts, vendor instruction-only authority; any vendor-custody model blocked pending counsel analysis.

title: Operator regulatory status is not tied to feature activation
description: Features can change the operator's status: investment model portfolios or advice for compensation (investment adviser; the Advisers Act §203(b)(4) charitable exemption covers the charity, not a for-profit vendor); transaction-based compensation on securities liquidation (broker-dealer); hosting solicitation for many charities (CA AB 488 platform registration); handling consumer financial data as a for-profit (GLBA/FTC Safeguards, including 16 CFR 314.4(j) 30-day notice to the FTC for 500+ consumers). UNB-RCN-ENT-014 covers identity regimes only.
impact: A configuration change silently creates an unlicensed activity.

title: Notification catalog lacks CAN-SPAM/TCPA legal classification and opt-out/revocation handling deadlines
description: CAN-SPAM applies to commercial email from any sender including nonprofits; transactional/relationship messages are largely exempt; opt-outs must be honoured within 10 business days (general knowledge). TCPA requires prior express consent for autodialed or prerecorded calls/texts to wireless numbers; the tax-exempt nonprofit exemption concerns telephone solicitation rules, and a for-profit operator sending on the sponsor's behalf may not share it (general knowledge).
impact: Statutory damages exposure (TCPA per-message) on SMS grant notifications.

title: E-SIGN consumer-consent question (Q10) applies to donor acknowledgments, not to grant agreements with organizations
description: §7001(c) consumer disclosures apply to consumers; charity grantees are organizations. Treating grant agreements like consumer records adds needless consent steps.
impact: Extra friction for ER/conditional grants.
proposed_resolution: Note in RR-UNB-GRANT-024-r1; keep Q10 for donor CWAs.

title: Counsel-approved rules have no authority-derived golden tests and no automatic sunset
description: Rev. Proc. 2017-53 §7 gives worked currency examples; §1.530A-7T expires 2029-09-30. UNB-RULE-001 records expiration but nothing deactivates an expired rule or proves the encoded rule reproduces the authority's examples.
impact: Silent misencoding of currency rules; expired temporary rules keep permitting distributions.

title: No entitlement model separate from sponsor policy and flags
description: The configuration catalog mixes contract scope (what a program bought) with sponsor policy (how a sponsor governs). No record states which optional capabilities a tenant/program is entitled to.
impact: Commercial disputes or tier changes can only be expressed by editing sponsor policy, risking changes to fiduciary behaviour; sales promises are unauditable.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-XIN-SAS-001 with NonRemovable fiduciary capabilities.

title: Feature-flag governance absent; flags are the usual path to hidden tenant forks
description: Requirements mandate one release for all cells but are silent on flags; inventory has no flag requirement.
impact: Ungoverned flags reintroduce per-tenant behaviour and break replay determinism.

title: Release rollout and schema migration fan-out across cells unspecified
description: One release to N cells with Strata lacking schema templating has no rollout order, halt criteria, version-skew limit or peak freeze.
impact: A bad migration can reach all sponsors at once, possibly during December peak.

title: Webhook subscription lifecycle missing
description: Signing and replay defense exist; registration, scope, delivery guarantees, redelivery and termination do not (TVS-411).
impact: Data flows after partner termination; overshared payloads.

title: Tenant envelope and cross-tenant correlation rule not mandated for events and telemetry
description: Isolation is required for streams/logs but no envelope field or cross-tenant causation prohibition exists; correlation IDs may be global.
impact: Leakage through telemetry/support tooling; migration equivalence unprovable; metering impossible.

title: No registration/consent model for third-party applications calling Unbound
description: Provider registry covers outbound integrations; inbound apps acting for sponsors or donors have no registration, scope or sponsor consent.
impact: Bespoke access grants; sponsor cannot see who reads donor data.

title: Distribution-partner exit with fund portability is undefined and invites ownership change by data migration
description: UNB-TEN-016 gives the partner an exportable dataset and portability protocol; RCF-ENT-012 identifies partner exit as a separate process but nothing defines it. Market evidence shows white-label programs and sponsors switch vendors (Ren iPhi 6 of 57 left). Without a requirement, a 'program migration' could move funds to a new sponsor by changing ownership data, bypassing sponsor A's exclusive legal control and donors' elections.
impact: Unauthorized transfer of charitable assets; donor lockout (TVF-135); tax reporting errors.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-XIN-SAS-007; refine UNB-TEN-016 so partners receive only sponsor-authorized data.

impact: Pricing of high-volume-low-balance and embedded models is guesswork.

title: Sandbox tenants lack isolation rules
description: No prohibition of production data copy or live-rail reach from sandboxes.
impact: PII exposure or real payments from test configurations.

title: No subprocessor register/notice to tenants
description: Vendor inventory is internal only.
impact: Sponsors cannot discharge vendor-risk duties.

title: Recovery objectives per capability are untestable; need data-class table
description: UNB-RES-003 asks each capability for RTO/RPO; REQ-X-006 sets RPO 0 for commits; TVS-607 shows inconsistent restore points across stores.
impact: Restores break payment gating; contracts promise unmeasured objectives.

title: Tenant lifecycle has no states or gates
description: Onboarding, suspension, exit spread across three documents.
impact: Tenants could go live without legal evidence; suspension semantics unclear.

title: Sponsor exit export/destruction not reconciled with append-only storage in a requirement
description: RCC-ENT-005 resolution (tenant-scoped chains, per-tenant key destruction, exit certificate) is not written into a requirement; UNB-TEN-016 names partner rather than sponsor.
impact: Exit becomes either impossible or destructive of others' integrity checkpoints.

title: API deprecation policy has no windows or obligations
description: Lists topics only.
impact: Partners cannot plan; sunsets may strand recommendations.

title: Platform vendor regulatory status varies by operating model (own-brand app vs white-label vs charity-side button)
description: daf-landscape analysis reads California §12599.9 as making an own-brand grant-recommendation app Type A and a licensed white-label portal Type E; the DAF exclusion names only the sponsor. Model selection therefore changes the platform company's own obligations, not just the sponsor's.
impact: D2C and embedded launches may trigger vendor registration and disclosure duties unplanned in requirements.
proposed_resolution: Record per-model vendor obligations in the applicability register (link OB-38); decision XID-SAS-005.

title: No operating model requires its own implementation; isolation profile choice is independent of model
description: Business-model analysis (business-models.jsonl) found every model servable by configuration, roles, adapters and view composition; none requires Profile C by nature. The remaining risk is the hybrid model mixing sponsor-direct and partner programs in one tenant, which RCD-004 resolves if tenant = legal sponsor.
impact: Building three profiles 'for the models' would be unjustified cost.
proposed_resolution: Keep RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 default-plus-gated approach; do not tie profile to model.

title: No identity realm separation
description: Workforce, partner workforce, customer and workload principals are not separated.
impact: Privilege bleed; partner exit lockout.

title: Operator workforce access outside sponsor authority (TVF-134 not adopted)
description: Operator JIT is approved by the operator; sponsors do not see access. Under outsourced/infrastructure models this places sponsor records under people the sponsor never delegated to.
impact: Breach of sponsor exclusive legal control; SOC2 privileged access gap.

title: Step-up rules scattered, partner-delegated and without freshness
description: No single matrix; partner CIBA confirmation accepted.
impact: ATO on payout-relevant changes.

title: Access reviews lack cadence and consequence
description: No auto-suspension; third-party registers not in scope.
impact: Stale privileges.

title: Break-glass controls exist only as findings
description: Scope, IdP independence, two-person activation and tenant notice are not requirements.
impact: Highest-impact privileged path uncontrolled.

impact: Spoliation exposure.

description: Evidence packages target auditors.
impact: Ad hoc database extracts under subpoena.

description: RR-REQ-X-036-r1 requires a review task at expiry; RCD-007 recommends class batches.
impact: Unbounded human work or inconsistent practice.

title: No durable timer/obligation mechanism
description: Deadlines are stated but not how they fire exactly once across restarts/restores.
impact: Missed Form 8282 windows; duplicate outreach.

title: In-flight process instances have no definition versioning
description: State-machine changes can strand instances.
impact: Stuck grants/migrations after release.

description: Every orchestration need found (timers, retries, compensation, human tasks, long-running state) is covered by in-DB state machines, outbox, timer table and the work queue, inside one transaction with the ledger. An engine would add a second durable store whose state must reconcile with the ledger.
impact: Avoids complexity contrary to UNB-TEC-002.

description: 529 G-45-like data set absent.
impact: Opaque white-label comparisons.

title: Migration cutover has no customer-facing transition window
description: Freeze effects are not communicated.
impact: December disruption; complaints.

description: Embedded checkout requirements do not forbid partner intermediary accounts.
impact: Custody/commingling and platform-law remittance duties.
