title: Print/mail chain of custody missing on check rail
description: No manifest reconciliation, mail evidence semantics or returned-mail rule.
impact: Duplicate or lost checks; stale addresses.

title: No shared cost attribution model behind the unit-economics KPIs
description: REQ-X-043 asks "what does each transaction, fund, sponsor and exception actually cost, including AI, vendors, custody, mailing, labor and rework" and lists "unit margin with explicit cost allocation assumptions", but no requirement defines cost pools, drivers, activities, cost objects, attribution rules, methods or confidence. UNB-ECO-001 names drivers for a planning model only.
impact: Every unit-cost KPI would be computed ad hoc per dashboard with different allocation assumptions; numbers will disagree and cannot be audited.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-XIN-ECO-001..004 (non-posting attribution ledger, canonical entities, method+confidence, GL reconciliation).

title: Management cost allocation sits inside the financial accounting requirement with no non-posting boundary
description: UNB-ACC-014 places "cost centers, allocation methodologies and scenario models" in the full accounting system and only distinguishes forecasts from actuals. It does not say that management cost allocations must never create journal entries, change fund balances or available-to-grant.
impact: An implementer could post activity-based allocations as journals, altering sponsor operating P&L or (worse) charging funds, without fee policy authority.
proposed_resolution: Refine UNB-ACC-014 (RR-UNB-ACC-014-r1): management attribution is a projection; only approved fee/billing (UNB-ACC-010) or CPA-approved functional allocation entries post.

title: No reconciliation of attributed cost to GL actuals and no explicit unallocated residual
description: REQ-X-043 requires "independent tie-out to approved financial statements" for metrics in general but no economics-specific reconciliation exists. Nothing prevents unattributable cost from being silently spread across cost objects via a plug driver.
impact: Unit costs can look precise while omitting or double counting cost; trends move because of allocation changes, not operations.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-004: monthly ReconciliationRun; UnallocatedResidual reported, tolerance-gated, never spread.

title: Cost figures carry no attribution confidence or uncertainty range
description: UNB-ECO-002 separates measured, benchmark, scenario and assumption inputs for planning models, but runtime cost figures have no method tag, confidence grade or range. TVC-020 records parameter drift (8% vs 10% exceptions; $103/h vs $90/h; $38.87-$86/h).
impact: Decision makers cannot tell a metered $0.30 ACH fee from a 50%-uncertain hosting allocation.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-003 grades A-D/U with ranges; dashboards show grade.

title: Capacity forecasting and SLA-based staffing are still unspecified despite known December backlog arithmetic
description: Economic-model §3 shows annual-average staffing leaves ~9,600 December cases taking ~223 working days to clear; TVF-060/TVF-162 are open. Work-queue requirements route existing work but no requirement forecasts arrivals by skill or computes staff needed for an SLA.
impact: Sponsors will breach grant SLAs every December and staff pressure will drive unsafe approvals (FMEA-14).
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-017 capacity forecast with skill pools and backlog simulation; forecast accuracy tracked.

title: AI cost budgets lack per-run attribution, estimate, and defined exhaustion behaviour
description: AIN-028 says bound budgets "without silently abandoning work" but does not define what happens on exhaustion during a control step, how run cost attaches to the grant/case, or whether a pre-execution estimate exists.
impact: Budget exhaustion could stall a sanctions/eligibility review or silently skip it; AI cost per grant is unknowable.

title: Single-denominator unit costs (cost per account) mislead; evidence shows cost per account rises with fund size
description: daf-landscape finds community-foundation cost per DAF account rises with size (elasticity 1.22) and warns "cost per account is not a scale-free unit"; the Ren/RCF per-end-year-fund ratio is explicitly not ARPU. REQ-X-043 KPIs do not require multiple denominators.
impact: Wrong pricing and segment conclusions.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-007 metric catalog mandates per-account-month, per-grant (by rail), per-$ AUM bps, per-resolved-case, with population and grade.

title: Configurable service charges to funds are not linked to attributed cost or to a legal reasonableness review
description: Fee schedules, waivers and pass-throughs exist (UNB-ACC-010, REQ-X-067) but nothing records the cost basis of a special-request charge (ED review, wire, stop-payment, complex asset liquidation) or requires counsel review of charges that exceed cost.
impact: Charges against charitable assets without documented basis may be challenged as unreasonable; or sponsors under-recover and cross-subsidise.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-018 recovery ratio reporting + decision XID-ECO-002 for counsel.

title: Cost targets have no binding counter-metric floors
description: REQ-X-043 cautions against optimising speed at the expense of compliance and ADV-577 names the risk, but no requirement makes a cost target conditional on configured floors for control effectiveness, compliance, SLA, accuracy and donor friction.
impact: Cost programmes can silently weaken controls; Goodhart effects.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-015/016: floors block ratchet and trigger rollback review.

title: No process mining over the full event log
description: REQ-X-042 learns from exceptions and near misses; the WQ Performance view has rework and time by stage. Inefficiency also lives in happy paths (waiting on providers, handoffs, touches on successful grants) which exception-driven learning never sees.
impact: Large waiting and handoff costs remain invisible.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-010 mining of domain events with control-step tagging.

title: No revenue attribution entity to compute profitability by segment/service model
description: REQ-X-067 item 5 says profitability analytics distinguish sponsor assets, adviser AUM, serviced AUM, flow and platform revenue but defines no RevenueRecord linking recognised revenue to cost objects and service models.
impact: Profitability by model (D2C vs white-label vs outsourced) cannot be computed consistently.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-012 RevenueRecord sourced from posted fee revenue only.

title: Pricing/service simulation exists only as design-time models with illustrative inputs
description: UNB-ENT-003 and UNB-ECO-005 require sensitivity and stress; Echelon DAF case reports "superior-at-expected" with mostly illustrative levers and an adverse corner that reverses savings. No runtime simulator consumes measured drivers.
impact: Pricing decisions continue on illustrative inputs after production data exists.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-013 scenario runs over measured parameter register with Echelon verdict vocabulary.

title: Cost data can disclose sponsor volumes and staff performance
description: Attributed costs embed volumes (grants, exceptions) per sponsor and time per worker. REQ-X-043 addresses benchmark reidentification (ADV-561) generally; HUMAN-WORK-QUEUES forbids ranking staff on raw speed. Neither covers cost views.
impact: Cross-sponsor leakage of commercially sensitive volumes; covert staff surveillance through cost-per-worker views.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-021 scoping, k-threshold benchmarks, no per-worker cost views.

title: Failure and recovery cost is not a category on the cost model
description: TVR-ECON-003 measures hours for post-payment reviews and incidents; the incident cost formula is proposed. No cost category aggregates failure/recovery cost alongside processing cost, so savings claims ignore failure cost changes.
impact: Automation that lowers handling cost but raises incident cost looks beneficial.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-002 CostPool type FailureAndRecovery; UNB-XIN-ECO-019 ROI includes it.

title: Statutory functional expense allocation and management activity costing are not distinguished
description: UNB-ACC-019 requires functional expenses where required (Form 990 Part IX). Management ABC will classify the same GL costs differently. No requirement keeps them as separate governed views over one activity dataset.
impact: Either management numbers leak into statutory filings without CPA review, or two inconsistent activity datasets emerge.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-001 states the boundary; XID-ECO-005 for CPA.

title: Real-time cost attribution would add infrastructure without decision value for most costs
description: Most cost pools (salaries, hosting, custody fees) are known only monthly. Only metered external calls (AI, payment rails, verification vendors) are knowable per event. A real-time attribution pipeline conflicts with minimal-infrastructure preference.
impact: Over-engineering; false precision on intra-month allocations.
proposed_resolution: Near-real-time only for metered grade-A costs; monthly for pools (UNB-XIN-ECO-005/004).

title: The cost-reduction loop lacks an independent verifier
description: TVR-ORG-004 places queue telemetry outside the queue owner; the same independence is needed for verifying claimed savings, otherwise the owner who benefits from a target certifies it.
impact: Self-certified savings.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-015 assigns verification to finance (FP&A) separate from the operations owner.

title: Cost-reduction targets could ratchet below the structural staffing / SoD floor
description: UNB-ECO-003 requires accounting for minimum responsible staffing; TVA-022/TVC-018 dispute the floor (6-8 vs ~20). A ratchet without a floor term will set unattainable targets or pressure SoD erosion.
impact: Targets incentivise removing segregation of duties.
proposed_resolution: Ratchet rule includes a configured structural floor (UNB-XIN-ECO-015).

title: Service-level tiers are not costed
description: REQ-X-071 item 5 names cost-to-serve and service-credit implications without method. SLA tier cost should come from capacity model at peak.
impact: SLA tiers sold below cost or unattainable in December.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-017 outputs staff-for-SLA; UNB-XIN-ECO-020 service-level economics.

title: Cost-based choices could override verified recipient payment facts
description: If cost forecasting is added naively (check vs ACH), a system might switch rails for cost. Recipient payment method must follow verified bank ownership and recipient preference.
impact: Funds misdirected to unverified accounts.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-ECO-008 quotes are advisory and cannot change rail selection rules.

title: Hypothesis framing 'financial and relationship management system' misstates who owns the assets
description: The tested hypothesis frames the DAF enterprise as a financial and relationship management system. In a DAF the sponsor has exclusive legal control of contributed assets (IRC 4966(d)(2) per BRIEF; UNB-ACC-005 'DAF subfund balances are not personally owned donor assets'). A relationship-management framing invites CRM-style customer ownership semantics (customer account = customer money) that are legally wrong and would let relationship data (preferences, notes, advisor role labels) be treated as authority.
impact: Relationship records could be used to authorize money movement or to infer donor ownership (refund requests, account 'transfers' by relationship owners).
proposed_resolution: Reformulate the hypothesis (see REPORT 'Hypothesis verdict'): authority facts (advisory privilege, successor designation, anonymity election, contributor of record) belong to Identity & Delegation and are append-only; relationship/engagement data is non-authoritative for money (UNB-XIN-EVA-014).

title: No event catalog declares authority class or required consistency
description: UNB-EVT-001 lists owner, schema, version, producer, actor, consumer, control, evidence and side-effect classification, and the GR-EVT envelope adds correlation/causation, but no catalog field says whether an event is an authoritative financial fact, an authoritative non-financial decision, a derived projection, an informational external observation or an AI observation, nor whether consumers may act on it eventually. The Echelon generator's EventContract has only Name/Data/Producer/Consumers/Capability.
impact: A consumer can gate a consequential command on an informational or derived event (e.g., PaymentExecutionAcknowledged treated as paid, ContributionAvailable treated as capacity).
proposed_resolution: Refine UNB-EVT-001 (RR-UNB-EVT-001-r1) to require authority, consistency, ordering scope, idempotency key formula, correction pattern and retention class per event; event-matrix.jsonl is the first instance (96 events).

title: Two candidate sources of financial truth: a generic append-only EventStore and the double-entry journal
description: The tenant-aware persistence design places all business facts in one 'Append-only EventStore' with projections, while the authoritative-data model says the ledger is the single authoritative source of balances, and daf-landscape strategy proposes an 'event-sourced ledger'. If financial domain events (FundingReservationCreated, GrantPayableRecognized, PaymentSettled) live in a generic store and the journal is a projection of them, there are two logs whose disagreement has no defined winner; if the journal is authoritative, an event store beneath it is redundant.
impact: Reconciliation between two internal logs becomes a permanent control; replay of domain events can regenerate journals under changed posting rules, rewriting financial history.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-XIN-EVA-001: the balanced journal is itself the financial event log; financial domain facts reference JournalBatchId; no balance is computed from any other log.

title: Universal 'current state = projection of immutable records' over-applies event sourcing to non-financial data
description: UNB-DATA-004 requires every current state to be a deterministic projection of immutable records and UNB-DATA-001 forbids UPDATE/DELETE of 'facts'. Applied to CRM preferences, interaction logs, notification delivery status, outbox status and work-queue assignment, this forces event sourcing where nothing financial or legal depends on replay, and collides with privacy erasure (UNB-DATA-007).
impact: Higher build and skill cost (upcasters, projection rebuilds) for modules that need only history; erasure becomes crypto-shredding of streams.
proposed_resolution: Refine UNB-DATA-004 (RR-UNB-DATA-004-r1) to three storage classes: authoritative-financial and authority facts append-only with in-transaction current state; non-financial relationship data mutable with system-versioned history; operational coordination state mutable.

title: Concurrent posting versus period close is unspecified
description: UNB-ACC-017 requires period locks, but no requirement says how a posting that is validating against an open period serializes against a concurrent hard close. Under snapshot isolation a posting can read 'open', the close commits, then the posting commits into a closed period (write skew; PostgreSQL docs show Serializable prevents this class of anomaly but requires retry on SQLSTATE 40001).
impact: Closed-period figures change after statements are issued; as-issued statements no longer tie to the ledger.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-002: postings lock the period row FOR SHARE; close takes it FOR UPDATE; effective dates in hard-closed periods route to PriorPeriodAdjustment.

title: Statements and reports are classed as eventual projections without a determinism watermark
description: The ownership matrix classes statements with dashboards as T3 eventual projections. Nothing requires a report to declare the ledger commit watermark it was computed from, so two runs during posting activity can differ, and auditors cannot reproduce a figure.
impact: Inconsistent financial results between statement, Schedule D package and management report for the same period.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-003: financial reports compute only from a FinancialSnapshotSealed (period, commit watermark); identical watermark gives identical figures.

title: Missing external files are indistinguishable from 'no activity'
description: Custodian position files, bank statements and BAI/return files, and IRS exempt-organization extracts arrive as batches. Requirements cover authenticity (UNB-EVT-003) and reconciliation (UNB-ACC-018) but not an expected-file calendar, control totals or gap detection. A missing return file means returns are silently unposted; a missing position file means capacity is computed on stale positions.
impact: Capacity overstated; late R-code returns discovered after statements; eligibility checks run on stale lists.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-004: per-source completeness watermark and gap detection; dependent automation holds when a source is behind.

title: Idempotency key derivation for external observations is unspecified; same key with different payload is silently dropped
description: UNB-GEX-003 requires idempotency but not the key formula. ACH has no end-to-end key (daf-landscape E9), so return matching depends on trace numbers; custodian corrections reuse references with changed amounts. A naive dedupe on key drops a corrected record.
impact: Corrected custodian or bank records discarded as duplicates; or duplicates double-posted when keys are random request ids.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-005: business-key registry per source; same key + different payload hash -> conflict case.

title: Durable timers and long-running workflow state have no requirement (DG-08)
description: Report 13 records DG-08 (durable scheduler/timer) as a gap with no requirement. Check aging (180 days), ACH return windows, liquidation tranches, multi-leg funding, cooling-off periods and revalidation all need durable waiting state and stuck detection.
impact: Lost timers after restart; workflows that never terminate; no route to human resolution.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-007: process managers as versioned rows with next_due_at, step idempotency, stall detection to a human-resolution queue. No external workflow engine.

title: Generating public schemas for every internal event couples internal refactoring to external API compatibility
description: UNB-RCN-ARC-001 generates JSON Schema for every inter-component event and checks breaking changes. If internal domain events are published to partners (webhooks, embedded widgets), every internal rename becomes a breaking external change, and partners begin depending on internal states (e.g., ProviderAcknowledged).
impact: Event schemas freeze the domain model; partners infer payment finality from internal events.
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-008: separate private domain events from a small published integration-event contract with explicit mapping and versioning; unknown versions fail closed for authoritative consumers.

title: 'Hold' is used for three legally different things
description: Compliance protective holds (stop money), sanctions blocks (funds must be blocked, not returned, TVCTL-13), fund disputes (ADM-023) and records legal holds (retention) are all called holds. A shared Hold abstraction risks a records legal hold freezing grants, or a fund freeze blocking inbound dividends and contributions.
impact: Over-blocking (charitable distributions halted by a litigation records hold) or under-blocking (OFAC block treated as release-to-fund).
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-010: distinct typed hold kinds with declared blocked command sets.

title: Batch-level approval semantics would release items after a mid-batch sanctions hit
description: Recurring-grant runs and payment files are naturally processed as batches. No requirement forbids a batch-level approval or dispatch decision. If a batch is approved as a unit, an OFAC listing published mid-run does not stop items not yet dispatched unless each item re-checks the hold version.
impact: Strict-liability sanctions exposure (REG-036 per existing register).
proposed_resolution: UNB-XIN-EVA-011: a batch is a container of independent item commands; each item release and each dispatch checks HoldPublicationVersion.

title: Sponsor-to-sponsor bulk moves risk being executed as tenant data migrations
description: Tenant migration (UNB-TEN-012) preserves identifiers and history in place; sponsor-to-sponsor transfer is a legal distribution (RR-UNB-WF-014-r1). With tenant = legal sponsor (RCD-004), moving 10,000 funds from sponsor A to sponsor B is 10,000 legal transfers across two sponsor databases, not a re-homing of event streams. No requirement covers sponsor-initiated bulk transfer or the boundary.
impact: Destination sponsor books would contain the source sponsor's historical postings as if its own; source books lose the distribution record.

title: Echelon-generated DAF architecture couples approval to accounting and payment through asynchronous events and collapses payment states
description: The Echelon generator emits GrantApprovalRecorded consumed by redemption, payment and accounting steps, and PaymentRecorded consumed by remittance and reconciliation; handoffs are 'replaced-by-event'. This contradicts REQ-X-022/TX-11 (approval + reservation atomic) and REQ-X-083 (orthogonal payment states).
impact: Generated architectures for the DAF case study would recommend eventual consistency for the reservation invariant.
proposed_resolution: Record conflict XIC-EVA-003; propose that the generator distinguish synchronous invariant steps from event handoffs (framework feedback; no change made to Echelon).

title: Communications are not revalidated against the current fact version before send
description: ADV-088 tests that a notification cannot claim Paid without confirmed state, but nothing handles the case where the fact changes between enqueue and send (R03 return after 'paid' email enqueued; anonymity election after remittance enqueued).
impact: False finality notices; anonymity leaks.

title: Scale exception gate lacks a quantified threshold
description: REQ-X-020 says a split requires reproducible measurements but gives no threshold. Volume arithmetic (REPORT) shows a Fidelity-scale sponsor (3.0m grants/yr) at an assumed year-end spike needs roughly 40-200 authoritative transactions per second, so the gate should be expressed against benchmarked capacity.
impact: Premature broker/service introduction or, conversely, no trigger when one is justified.

title: Correction propagation to derived records is stated but not enumerated
description: UNB-DATA-005 requires preserving the 'effect on derived balances, grants, filings and notices' but no registry lists which derived records depend on which facts: fee accruals on AUM, unit allocations on NAV, acknowledgments on completed-gift valuation, Form 8282 on lots, statements on snapshots, Schedule D aggregates.
impact: Corrections fix the journal but leave stale fees, units and acknowledgments.

title: Three divergent event naming schemes for the same payment facts
description: GR-EVT-045 PaymentInstructionSubmissionRecorded, TVR-EVT-001 PaymentSubmitted/PaymentFinal/PaymentStatusUnknown and the Echelon PaymentRecorded name the same or overlapping facts. GEX-ADR-001 is open.
impact: Consumers bind to the wrong event; matrix and tests disagree.
proposed_resolution: Use event-matrix.jsonl crosswalk (existing_ids) as the input to GEX-ADR-001.

title: AI/fact separation is a policy statement without an enforcement mechanism
description: UNB-EVT-005 forbids raw agent output from emitting state-changing events, and the ownership matrix says AI owns no facts by assertion, but nothing makes it impossible: no type separation, no database-role separation, no promotion record.
impact: Prompt injection or tool misuse could append a fact through a shared append API.
proposed_resolution: RR-UNB-EVT-005-r1: Observation / Proposal / Command / Fact types; AI role has INSERT only on ai_observation schema.

title: Conflicting-instruction detection has no conflict scope or precedence rules
description: ADM-023 says detect conflicting directions and hold; TVS-370 covers a disputed transfer-out. There is no definition of what makes two instructions conflict (same fund? same charity? standing vs one-off?) and no rule for the race between an instruction and an authority epoch change (successor notice while a grant is in flight).
impact: Either everything is flagged (queue flood) or opposite instructions both execute.

title: Blanket append-only rule contradicts the outbox and process state the architecture depends on
description: UNB-DATA-001 forbids UPDATE/DELETE of committed authoritative records; UNB-EVT-002 requires a durable outbox, which must record delivery attempts and status, and process managers must move state. If outbox and process rows are deemed authoritative they cannot be updated; if they are append-only, dispatch claiming via row locks (SKIP LOCKED) does not work.
impact: Implementers either violate UNB-DATA-001 or build an unnecessarily complex append-only queue.
proposed_resolution: Classify outbox, leases, timers and work-queue assignment as operational coordination state (mutable, audited) in RR-UNB-DATA-004-r1; conflict XIC-EVA-002.

title: Correlation is defined per grant event envelope but not across capabilities
description: The GR-EVT envelope carries correlationId and causationId, but service cases, AI observations, communications, custodian file items and fee recomputations are outside that catalog. A multi-investment grant spans redemption legs, payments, returns, cases and notices; a succession notice spawns holds on many grants. Without a shared correlation root and business-key set, cross-function questions ('everything caused by this ACH return') require heuristic joins.
impact: Incomplete exception dossiers and audit reconstruction; AI summaries built on guessed links.

title: One generic event table for all record kinds would mix authority classes
description: The tenant-aware design draws a single append-only EventStore with JSON payloads for every business fact. A single table holding journal-relevant facts, AI observations, notifications and CRM changes makes database-level privilege separation (AI role cannot insert facts), per-class retention, per-class indexing and balanced-journal CHECK constraints impossible, and pushes integrity into application code.
impact: Weaker enforcement of financial invariants and AI separation; retention and erasure per class become filters over one table.

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: CAN-SPAM/TCPA message classification
description: Two agents independently specified per-message-type legal classification (commercial vs transactional; TCPA consent class) with sender legal entity and opt-out handling. REG-003 is P1, CRM-003 is P0.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: CRM-003 is canonical (it adds sender legal entity and send-time suppression keyed by sender). Fold REG-003's counsel-approval and revocation-handling clauses into CRM-003 at adoption; REG-003 is retained only as a traceability alias. Priority: P0 only for SMS/voice (statutory damages); email classification P1 (see XID-INT-001).

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: unclaimed property for uncashed grant checks
description: BNK-007 specifies a counsel-approved per-state rule table and outreach before stale-dating; NPG-011 specifies the jurisdiction priority rule (payee address state, then holder state). They are two halves of one rule.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: Keep both: BNK-007 is canonical for the rule table and lifecycle; NPG-011 is canonical for jurisdiction selection and MUST be referenced by BNK-007 as its jurisdiction function. One scenario must exercise both (XDS-BNK and XDS-NPG escheat scenarios are linked).

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: bulk movement of funds between legal sponsors
description: SAS-007 (partner exit with fund portability) and EVA-009 (TransferProgram process manager) both require per-fund independent transfer grants approved by the originating sponsor and forbid tenant-migration shortcuts.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: EVA-009 is the mechanism (process manager, per-fund DAF transfer, no LegalSponsorId update); SAS-007 is the case and donor-election front end that invokes it. Adoption must state SAS-007 depends_on EVA-009 and share one reconciliation identity (elected = transferred + declined + remaining).

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: seasonal capacity and December staffing forecast
description: SVC-008 requires a seasonal capacity plan for live service channels; ECO-017 requires a 13-week and December forecast for every skill pool including service.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: ECO-017 is canonical. SVC-008's channel-specific inputs (Erlang-C for live channels, callback conversion) become a method option inside ECO-017 for live-channel pools only.

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: journal authority over derived re-derivation
description: EVA-001 states balances and reports are computed only from the insert-only journal; ACC-003 states posted journals are authoritative and never regenerated, with re-derivation run only as a comparison control.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: Complementary, not redundant: EVA-001 canonical for 'single financial log'; ACC-003 canonical for the re-derivation control. Both must be adopted together; neither alone closes the replay-reposting risk (RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1).

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: durable process managers, timers and in-flight versioning
description: EVA-007 defines persisted process managers with timers and stall detection; WFA-001 defines DueObligation timers firing exactly once across restore; WFA-002 defines definition versioning per in-flight instance.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: EVA-007 canonical for the process-manager model; WFA-001 and WFA-002 are retained as its timer and versioning clauses. Adoption merges them into one specification with one test suite.

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: funds-flow title and exclusion of partners from the money path
description: REG-001 requires a FundsFlow declaration naming the legal title holder of every account; OTH-003 requires grant payments to flow from sponsor-controlled accounts without partner or host intermediation; ERP-004 separates grant payees from operating vendors.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: REG-001 canonical for title; OTH-003 is its payment-path corollary and should be merged into REG-001 at adoption. ERP-004 is distinct (payee registry separation) and stays separate.

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: cost and usage metering feeds
description: Four agents specified source-specific cost or usage records: SAS-009 UsageRecord (infrastructure, API, AI), BNK-005 CostDriver facts (payments), ECO-005 VendorCostRecord (FOCUS), ERP-006 effort tagging of work items. ECO-002 defines the canonical cost entities.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: ECO-002 is the canonical model. SAS-009, BNK-005, ECO-005 and ERP-006 are feeds that MUST map into ActivityEvent/VendorCostRecord with one shared cost-object key set (tenant, program, fund, grant, case, AI run). Field names must be unified at adoption (XIC-INT-002).

title: Duplicate or overlapping requirements: party identity and relationship data classes
description: CRM-001 requires a minimal party identity core with capacity-scoped profiles; EVA-014 requires relationship data split into authority facts and engagement data that never authorizes money.
impact: Two specifications of one rule drift apart and give implementers conflicting acceptance criteria.
proposed_resolution: Complementary: EVA-014 canonical for authority vs engagement classification; CRM-001 canonical for PII partitioning by capacity. Adopt together; the identity core is an authority-class record.
